evidence.quote:
Now, there was an old manor-house, where they no longer ate snails, they
      were quite extinct; but the burdocks were not extinct, they grew and grew
      all over the walks and all the beds; they could not get the mastery over
      them
      it was a whole forest of burdocks.
evidence.paraphrase: The custom of eating snails has ended and the garden has become an overgrown forest of burdocks.

evidence.quote:
I am very
      happy to think that we have our good house, and the little one has his
      also! There is more done for us than for all other creatures, sure enough;
      but can you not see that we are folks of quality in the world?
evidence.paraphrase: Mother Snail expresses satisfaction and a belief that the snails are privileged above all creatures.

evidence.quote:
I should like to know how far it extends, and what there is
      outside!
evidence.paraphrase: Mother Snail voices curiosity about the extent of the world and what lies beyond it.

evidence.quote:
The old white snails were the first persons of distinction in the world,
      that they knew; the forest was planted for their sake, and the manor-house
      was there that they might be boiled and laid on a silver dish.
evidence.paraphrase: The snails regard themselves as the most important beings and believe the world exists for their sake, contrasting with the reader's knowledge.

evidence.quote:
There is nothing at all,
      said Father Snail. 
      No place can be better than
      ours, and I have nothing to wish for!
evidence.paraphrase: Father Snail insists there is nothing beyond their world and he desires nothing more.

evidence.quote:
they were never boiled, and never came on the silver
      dishes; so from this they concluded that the manor-house had fallen to
      ruins, and that all the men in the world were extinct; and as no one
      contradicted them, so, of course it was so.
evidence.paraphrase: From never being boiled, the snails infer that the manor-house is ruined and all humans are extinct, and their conclusion stands unchallenged.

evidence.quote:
And the rain beat on the
      dock-leaves to make drum-music for their sake, and the sun shone in order
      to give the burdock forest a color for their sakes; and they were very
      happy, and the whole family was happy; for they, indeed were so.
evidence.paraphrase: The snails believe the rain and sun exist for their benefit, a self-centered worldview presented for the reader to notice.
